relevance_reason: The paper first describes adult-onset autosomal dominant leukodystrophy without amyloid angiopathy, caused by truncating CST3 variants.

findings.statement: Bergner et al. (2024) described a new adult-onset leukodystrophy caused by dominant stop-gain or frameshift variants in the CST3 gene. Its clinical and radiologic features differed markedly from Icelandic cerebral amyloid angiopathy, which is caused by the p.Leu68Asn substitution in CST3.
quotes: We describe a novel adult onset leukodystrophy in 16 patients from eight families carrying one of four different stop-gain or frameshift dominant variants in the CST3 gene.
Clinical and radiological features differ markedly from the previously described Icelandic cerebral amyloid angiopathy found in patients carrying p.Leu68Asn substitution in CST3.

findings.statement: Bergner et al. (2024) reported 16 patients from 8 families with an adult-onset leukodystrophy. Patients had recurrent episodes of hemiplegic migraine with transient one-sided focal deficits. Motor symptoms and cognitive decline progressed slowly in mid to older adulthood. In some patients, a sudden clinical deterioration led to a long episode of reduced consciousness and even early death.
quotes: The clinical phenotype consists of recurrent episodes of hemiplegic migraine associated with transient unilateral focal deficits and slowly progressing motor symptoms and cognitive decline in mid to older adult ages.
In addition, in some cases acute onset clinical deterioration led to a prolonged episode with reduced consciousness and even early death.

findings.statement: Bergner et al. (2024) described characteristic MRI changes at typical predilection sites. These involved the deep cerebral white matter, sparing a rim of periventricular and directly subcortical tissue. Other sites were the middle blade of the corpus callosum, the posterior limb of the internal capsule, the middle cerebellar peduncles, the cerebral peduncles and, specifically, the globus pallidus.
quotes: Radiologically, pathognomonic changes are found at typical predilection sites involving the deep cerebral white matter sparing a periventricular and directly subcortical rim, the middle blade of corpus callosum, posterior limb of the internal capsule, middle cerebellar peduncles, cerebral peduncles and specifically the globus pallidus.

findings.statement: Bergner et al. (2024) studied 2 autopsy cases. Histopathology showed no angiopathy but did show micro- to macrocystic degeneration of the white matter. Astrocytes were activated at early stages and later showed severe degeneration and loss. Despite the loss of myelin, oligodendrocytes were increased in number and some were apoptotic.
quotes: Histopathologic characterization in two autopsy cases did not reveal angiopathy, but instead micro- to macrocystic degeneration of the white matter.
Astrocytes were activated at early stages and later displayed severe degeneration and loss.
In addition, despite the loss of myelin, elevated numbers of partly apoptotic oligodendrocytes were observed.

findings.statement: Bergner et al. (2024) identified 4 different heterozygous stop-gain or frameshift variants in the CST3 gene in 16 patients from 8 families with adult-onset leukodystrophy. A structural comparison of the variants suggested that specific truncations of cystatin C cause abnormal protein function, possibly by making the protein more prone to aggregation. The authors noted that further studies are needed to confirm this effect.
quotes: We describe a novel adult onset leukodystrophy in 16 patients from eight families carrying one of four different stop-gain or frameshift dominant variants in the CST3 gene.
A structural comparison of the variants in CST3 suggests that specific truncations of cystatin C result in an abnormal function, possibly by rendering the protein more prone to aggregation.
